chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who visits the House before shaving, he said: It is not befitting unless he is forgetful. } }, {

Then he said: Indeed, people came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the day of sacrifice, and some of them said: O Messenger of Allah, I shaved before I slaughtered; and some said: I shaved before I threw (the pebbles). So they did not leave anything that it was befitting for them to delay except that they brought it forward, so he said: There is no harm.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim shaves his head before throwing the pebbles during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between 'not befitting' (la yanbaghi) and 'sinful' (haram) regarding the sequence of Hajj rituals, establishing that minor deviations do not invalidate the pilgrimage. It links the Imami ruling directly to the Prophetic precedent, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) declared 'no harm' (la haraj) upon companions who had prematurely shaved or thrown pebbles, emphasizing ease in religious practice. This supports the Shia juristic principle that the prescribed order is recommended but not strictly obligatory for validity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from jameel Bin Darraj who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who visited the House (Kabah) before he shaved off (his head). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not befitting unless he happens to have forgotten’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said that: ‘Some people came over to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> on the day of the sacrifice, so one of them said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! I shaved off (my head) before I slaughtered’; and one of them said, ‘I shaved off (my head) before I pelted (the Rocks)’. So they did not leave anything which was befitting for that they should be delaying it, except that they brought it forward. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Nothing wrong’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who visits the House before shaving his head. He (the Imam) said, ’It is not proper unless it is because of forgetfulness.’

He (the Imam) then said, ’People came to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, on the day of al-Nahr (slaughtering the offering, 10th of Dhu al-Hajjah). Certain ones among them said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, I shaved before slaughtering my offering.’ Another one said, ‘I shaved before throwing pebbles.’ They did not leave anything that they were required to do later but that they had done it first. He (the Messenger of Allah) said it is not harmful.’”
